value.body: Electrical & Electronics Engineering (also offered as Electrical Engineering) covers circuits, electrical machines, power systems, power electronics, control systems and measurements, with some electronics and programming. It leads to the power, energy, manufacturing and electric-vehicle sectors, and to government utilities.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: You choose the branch at counselling, after the entrance exam. JEE Advanced rank is used for IITs; JEE Main rank for NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutes — all allotted through JoSAA. State colleges use state counselling with a state CET (EAMCET, MHT-CET, KCET, WBJEE and others) or, in Tamil Nadu (TNEA), Class 12 marks. Private universities may run their own tests. Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics is required.

value.title: At a glance
items: Power utilities and electricity-sector PSUs are a common employer; several recruit through GATE (EE paper).
UPSC Engineering Services (ESE) has an Electrical Engineering stream.
Overlap with electronics means some graduates move into embedded or software roles.
Common next steps: a core job, GATE → PSU / M.Tech, or state electricity board exams.
